findings.description: The security group allows inbound TCP port 22 (SSH) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the management interface of the instance to the entire internet and enabling brute-force or credential attacks.

Port 80 is open to 0.0.0.0/0, allowing unrestricted public access to the web server; while HTTP may be intended to be public, combined with unrestricted egress and no compensating controls this expands the attack surface unnecessarily.
AWS access key and secret access key are hardcoded in plaintext in the instance user_data script, which is visible via the EC2 metadata service and Terraform state, resulting in credential leakage.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true, so data stored on the volume is unencrypted at rest and could be exposed if the underlying storage is compromised or the snapshot is shared.
The EBS snapshot inherits the unencrypted state of the source volume, meaning backup data is also stored without encryption, risking exposure if the snapshot is inadvertently shared or accessed.
The S3 bucket used to store VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration, leaving potentially sensitive network traffic metadata unencrypted at rest.

The bucket has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block or bucket policy restricting public access, and force_destroy is enabled, so combined with default ACLs this could allow the bucket or its contents to be exposed publicly.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, automatically assigning public IP addresses to any instance launched in this subnet, increasing exposure to the internet.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, automatically assigning public IP addresses to any instance launched in this subnet, increasing exposure to the internet.
